wu: Routine Charades: Teacher mimes waking up, eating breakfast, going to school. Students shout the verbs (wake up, eat, go). Teacher writes them on the board.
wuAlt: Verb Tennis: Teacher says 'wake up', student says 'eat breakfast', teacher says 'go to school', student says 'study English'.
Quick Survey: Teacher asks 'What time do you wake up?' to 3 students, writes answers on the board.
pres: Teacher shows flashcards of a school day (7:00 wake up, 8:00 go to school, 10:00 have a break, 1:00 eat lunch, 4:00 go home). Models 'I wake up at 7 o'clock' and 'You wake up at 7 o'clock'. Checks understanding by asking 'What time do you wake up?' to a student.
presAlt: Storytime: Teacher tells a simple story about 'Ali's School Day' using the flashcards and gestures.
Realia: Teacher shows a real alarm clock and says 'I wake up at 7 o'clock'.
prac: Verb Drill Tennis: Students stand in two lines. Teacher says 'I wake up at...', student in the other line says 'You wake up at...'. Continue with 'go to school', 'have a break', 'eat lunch', 'go home'.
pracAlt: Routine Survey Mingle: Students walk around asking 'What time do you...?' for 3 routines, write answers on a grid.
Daily Timeline Drawing: Students draw a timeline of their school day and label times with 'at...'.
ls: Listen and Order: Teacher reads a short script about 'Leila's School Day' (e.g., 'I wake up at 7. I go to school at 8. I have a break at 10. I eat lunch at 1. I go home at 4.'). Students cut and paste 5 picture cards in the correct order.
re: Routine Relay: Two lines of students. Teacher says a routine (e.g., 'wake up'), first student runs to the board, writes the verb, runs back. Next student does the next one. Fastest team wins.
prod: My School Day Presentation: Students work in pairs. They draw 4 pictures of their school day and write a sentence for each (e.g., 'I wake up at 7 o'clock. I go to school at 8 o'clock. I eat lunch at 1 o'clock. I go home at 4 o'clock.'). They present to the class.
rw: Read and Find: Students read a short text about 'Youssef's Day' (e.g., 'Youssef wakes up at 7 o'clock. He goes to school at 8 o'clock. He has a break at 10 o'clock. He eats lunch at 1 o'clock. He goes home at 4 o'clock.'). They underline all the time expressions (at 7 o'clock, etc.).
st: Song: Sing 'What Time Do You...?' to the tune of 'Frère Jacques'. End with the routine: 'Today we learned to talk about our school day. Thank you, class!'
g: Students volley present simple sentences back and forth in pairs.
Students ask 'What time do you...?' to classmates and write answers.
Students draw a timeline of their school day with time expressions.
Students listen to a script and order picture cards of a daily routine.
Teams race to write present simple verbs on the board.
Students draw and present their daily routine in 4 sentences.
Students read a text and underline time expressions.
Students sing a song about daily routines.
Recap: 'Today we can describe our school day. Thank you, class!'
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a 6-sentence paragraph about their ideal school day.
Support / weaker learners: Use a sentence frame: 'I ______ at ______ o'clock.' for 4 routines.
hw: Write your real school day in 6 sentences (e.g., 'I wake up at 6:30. I eat breakfast at 7:00. I go to school at 7:30. I have a break at 10:00. I eat lunch at 1:00. I go home at 4:00.')
Draw a picture of your school day and label 3 activities with time expressions.
Ask a family member about their daily routine and write 3 sentences about it.
tip: Use gestures for all verbs to support visual and kinesthetic learners. For the American Space Oujda context, connect the topic to local school schedules (e.g., 'In Morocco, we have a long lunch break at 1 o'clock').
